text: A plan's check runs only its acceptance tests of the packages the plan touches (#487). It replaces D-0503, which also left out gofmt and go vet. Before a built-in Go plan is proposed, the planner's check tool and the factory's own check compile only the packages that hold its acceptance tests, and their test phase runs only those tests before their replay; gofmt and go vet still run, and the other tests of every package the plan touches run in a build's checks. What a plan's check decides never read those tests: it refuses an acceptance test that already passes, a deadline, an interruption or unfinished acceptance evidence, so they could refuse a draft only through their own time-outs, as they did #669's on 11-06 and #947's on 11-19. #947's check ran more than 770 tests of the three packages it touched before its seven acceptance tests, and ran out of its twelve minutes beside three other sandboxes on the same machine, after the agent's own check of the same plan had passed in 6 minutes 16 seconds. On main, with a cold cache and no other sandbox, the check of a plan shaped like #947's took 3 minutes 16 seconds before the change and 52 seconds after. Keeping gofmt, vet and the replay keeps the runner's evidence rules and #397's tests of them; only the tests that pinned the old rule, that an existing test's time-out refuses a draft, changed. A configured repository's base check still runs each touched part's commands before its selectors.
